clue.text: Stem appears to be favourite among the men

indicators.note: the stem and appears are to become something else, so their letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A plant stem seems to be the pick of the bunch among the male specimens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' signals that STEM APPEARS turns into another phrase: its eleven letters rearrange exactly into the name. PETE SAMPRAS was the top seed and favourite in men's tennis in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The American player dominated the men's game, so he was the bookmakers' pick in the men's draw.

clue.text: Permit after dinner request?

definitions.meaning: a travel document that allows its holder to cross borders
at a formal dinner a diner asks a neighbour to hand on the decanter of fortified wine

explanation.definitionFit: A travel document grants entry abroad, and the phrase also splits into the table request to send the port bottle round.

clue.text: Business not on exchange

parts.note: trade means commerce or business
a switch that is not on is off

explanation.surface: A firm that is not trading on the stock exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise in which one benefit is given up for another is a swap of advantages.

clue.text: Minister to be adequate

definitions.meaning: to minister to someone is to attend to their needs
something that will do the job is said to suffice for the purpose

explanation.definitionFit: To wait on someone is to attend them, and an object that suffices is said to 'do' for its purpose.

clue.text: Dole out a church weapon

indicators.note: the doling word stretches out around the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to dole out is to mete out, distribute in portions

explanation.surface: A parish hands out benefits and a church arms itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts A and CH inside METE, a synonym of 'Dole', giving M-A-CH-ETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation, and also as an arm in combat.

clue.text: Fix rent for small grower

parts.note: to root something is to fix it firmly in place
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A landlord sets a rent, maybe for a small tenant farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny secondary root growing from a plant's main root system.

clue.text: Lamb's uncle, perhaps and what he may have worn

definitions.meaning: an uncle of a young lamb is a relative among the flock of grown animals
the woolly hide of a ewe or ram, used for a coat

explanation.definitionFit: Split as SHEEP'S KIN it names a lamb's relations; whole, it is the woolly pelt such a relative wears.

clue.text: All this ready-to be won by I perhaps.

definitions.meaning: the phrase 'all ...' means ready, with this word standing for the second part

definitions.text: to be won by I perhaps.
definitions.meaning: a tennis player, such as the speaker, may win a section of a match made up of games

explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a match is divided into sets, each won by one player; 'I' stands for any player who could win one.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All set' means prepared, and a group of games in tennis is the unit a player wins on the way to the match.

clue.text: Not moved by this description about something shabby

indicators.note: the Latin word goes round, or about, the shabby item

parts.note: sic is the Latin word printed after a quotation to mean 'thus', i.e. as described
tat is cheap, shabby goods

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by an account of a shabby object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TAT inside SIC, giving S-TAT-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless or stationary has not been moved from its place.

clue.text: Attempt to include gorge in the agreement

indicators.note: the attempt word is made to hold the next piece within it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to gorge is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A diplomat tries to slip a gorge, a valley, into the terms of an accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts EAT inside TRY, giving TR-EAT-Y. 'gorge' looks like a noun, a ravine, but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pact signed between nations is a written accord.

clue.text: Rung about it as first recourse

indicators.note: the two little words it and as are turned about into a new order
first means only the opening letter of recourse is used

explanation.surface: A climber grabs a ladder rung as the first thing to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges IT AS into STAI, then 'first' adds the R from the start of 'recourse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a flight, like a rung on a ladder, is one level climbed.

clue.text: Help couple

definitions.meaning: to help is to work along with someone
to couple is to join, so read as ... it means operate together

explanation.definitionFit: Assisting means working jointly, and joining up two parts is operating them as a pair.

clue.text: Disjointed postwar feast, by the sound of it

indicators.note: these words say the feast phrase is only heard, not spelt as written

parts.note: a dinner held when fighting ends would be a meal of peace

explanation.surface: A rambling, patchy banquet thrown after a war.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACE and PIECE are pronounced the same, so a meal for peace sounds like the word for bit-by-bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piece by piece rather than as a whole, so fragmentary and unconnected.

clue.text: Tip the head

definitions.meaning: the sharp end of a pencil or blade
a headland, a promontory jutting into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp end is a tip, and a promontory such as Start Point is a coastal head.

clue.text: He has the last word in any court case

definitions.text: He has the last word in any court case

parts.words: He has the last word in any court case
parts.note: reads like a judge in a lawsuit, but the court is a sports court and the official's ruling is final

explanation.walkthrough: 'court case' suggests law; on a tennis or squash court the official in the chair makes the final call.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports umpire or official settles disputes on the field, and the ruling stands.

clue.text: Bounder has crazy backing for Dutch port

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, a rotter

indicators.note: backing means the word for crazy is turned to run backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A cad with a mad backer heads for a harbour in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns MAD into DAM, which follows ROTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest harbour in Europe, a seaport city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Sound steel pick

definitions.meaning: steel sounds like steal, which means to grab or pocket
to pick something is to choose it and carry it off

explanation.walkthrough: The first half needs two steps: 'steel' heard as STEAL, and steal means to help oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is helping yourself to goods, and choosing an item from a selection is selecting one.

clue.text: Uses opal to fix engagement

indicators.note: to fix the letters is to set them right in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone uses a gemstone to secure a betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fix' rearranges USES OPAL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal betrothal, the promise to marry.

clue.text: Fit to create year's hit

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are used to create a different word

explanation.surface: A hit record is made to become the song of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to create' rearranges YEARS HIT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of uncontrolled emotion, such as panic or wild laughter.

clue.text: We hear Berkshire town is the singer's second, so it becomes his first.

definitions.text: We hear Berkshire town is the singer's second, so it becomes his first.

parts.words: We hear Berkshire town is the singer's second, so it becomes his first.
parts.note: the Berkshire town Reading sounds like Redding, the surname of a soul singer, so the clue wants the singer's given name

explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, a county west of London; it sounds like Redding, the second name of the soul singer whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The soul star of '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' had Redding as surname and this as first name.

clue.text: Southern Royal Marine has a brainwave to provide a suitable weapon

parts.note: a brainwave is an idea
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A commando from the south thinks of a good gun to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol worn at the hip, suited to being carried at one's side.

clue.text: Little Indian saint lay about in front of the couch? Champion!

indicators.note: the first name is placed in front of the sofa word
the word lay goes about, or around, the next pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a little Indian is the short form IND
a davenport is a large sofa, chiefly in American usage

explanation.surface: A tiny Indian holy man lies down before a sofa, and a cheer goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IND and S inside LAY, giving L-INDS-AY; 'in front of' places this before DAVENPORT, an American word for a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: The American player won Wimbledon and was ranked world number one, so a tennis winner.

clue.text: American advocate of equality has the Spanish in a switch

indicators.note: the Spanish article is placed in the switch word

parts.note: a lever is a handle that works as a switch
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A US egalitarian is wired to a Spanish switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EL inside LEVER, giving LEV-EL-ER. The single L is the American spelling, hence 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who wants all people made equal in rank, named after the 17th-century English radicals.

clue.text: List the song

definitions.meaning: to list items is to count them off or give each a figure
a piece of music performed in a show or concert

explanation.definitionFit: Enumerating items gives each a figure, and a show's songs are individual items on its programme.

clue.text: Transport about five or skip around

annotationWithheld.why: Transport about five or skip around (6): CART round V and OR would need a T and give CAVORRT; no reading of 'or' gives O alone, so the wordplay as held does not make the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Transport about five or skip around

clue.text: Britain given a South-Eastern order

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom, Britain

explanation.surface: Britain is handed a command for the south-east region.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by a Russian tsar, so an edict.

clue.text: See 20
In Indiana, Bobby is a governor

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of letters Indiana Bobby

explanation.surface: A man called Bobby holds office as governor in Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside 'IndiaNA BOBby', where the five letters run across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: A provincial ruler in Mughal India, later any very wealthy man.

clue.text: Liberal shadow-is something of a sheep

parts.note: broad means liberal, tolerant, as in broad-minded
to tail someone is to shadow them

explanation.surface: A Liberal shadow minister turns out to be a bit of a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shadow' looks like a shadow cabinet post, but is a verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The glossy wavy fleece of a karakul lamb, so a part of one of these animals.

clue.text: …but rattling a sabre is more cowardly

indicators.note: rattling shakes the word sabre so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who rattles his sword is really the more cowardly one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattling' rearranges SABRE. The ellipsis ties the clue to the one before it on the page; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low and ignoble, and its comparative describes greater cowardice.

clue.text: Brother loses his head and the lady? Rubbish!

indicators.note: the brother word loses, gives up, a run of its letters
his head means the opening letter of the brother word is taken off

parts.note: taken as written; that the remaining letters also run inside the word is a coincidence, as the clue works by removing letters
her is the pronoun for the lady

explanation.surface: A brother is beheaded and loses his wife too, and someone exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his head' takes B off BROTHER, and 'loses' removes HER, leaving ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or drivel, said as an exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: Reminders of an oilier mamba

indicators.note: the reminders are made of the letters of oilier mamba, rearranged

explanation.surface: A slippery snake brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of OILIER MAMBA rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Collected objects that bring back the past, such as souvenirs of a famous person.
